tasks.title: P1: Enforce admin role on user routes server-side
tasks.description: Today any logged-in user can create, promote or delete users, including the admin. Enforce roles in the API.
tasks.details:
server/index.js: authenticateToken only at GET/POST /api/users, PUT/DELETE /api/users/:id (~lines 112, 217, 271, 304). Add requireAdmin middleware. Rules: only admin lists/creates/updates/deletes users; a user may read and change only their own password; nobody can change their own role; the last admin cannot be deleted or demoted. Take the role from the verified token, never from the request body.

[2026-10-29T20:41:44-04:00] plan: server/index.js only (+ new server/test/users-roles.test.js). Add requireAdmin (re-reads users.json so a demoted/deactivated admin loses access immediately; token role not trusted alone). GET/POST /api/users, DELETE: admin only. GET/PUT /api/users/:id: admin or self; self may change only password; admin may change fullName/role/isActive/password via allow-list (no passwordHash/id mass-assignment); nobody changes own role/isActive; last active admin cannot be deleted/demoted/deactivated; self-delete refused (UI already says 'Cannot delete yourself'). Frontend only fetches users when admin, so no UI breakage. Note: useAuth still calls init-admin on load -> task 4 must remove that call.

[2026-10-29T20:44:16-04:00] result: requireAdmin + self/admin rules implemented; 6 new API tests (16 total) pass. Same tests against the OLD index.js: failures (confirms they test the fix). Decisions: role verified against stored user, not token alone; admin can't change own role/isActive; self-delete refused. Drift check: only server/index.js + new test; no frontend change needed.
tasks.testStrategy: API tests: operator token gets 403 on create/promote/delete user and on self-promotion; admin succeeds; deleting the last admin is refused

subtasks.title: Server store: atomic writes, write queue, revisions
subtasks.description: Safe file writes and conflict detection for every JSON collection.
subtasks.details:
New server/store.js: write temp file then rename; per-file promise queue so read-modify-write cannot interleave; revision number kept beside each collection (rf_x.rev.json or wrapper-free sidecar so existing files stay readable); /api/data/:key POST accepts optional baseRevision and returns 409 if stale; GET returns revision in a header. Replace writeJSONFile use for data keys, users and bin locks.

[2026-10-29T21:46:46-04:00] plan: server/store.js (new): enqueue per-file promise chain; atomic write = JSON.stringify first (so bad data can't touch disk), temp file in same dir, fsync, rename, unlink temp on failure; revision = sha1(file bytes)[:16] (or 'none') so there is no sidecar that can disagree with the data; API: readJSON, readWithRevision, writeJSON(file,data,{baseRevision}) -> 409-able ConflictError, locked(file, tx=>...), update(file, fn). index.js: readJSONFile/writeJSONFile become store wrappers; users routes (create/put/delete, login lastLogin+hash upgrade) and bin-lock routes run read-modify-write inside the lock (login now updates the FRESH record instead of writing back a stale snapshot, which could clobber a concurrent admin edit). /api/data/:key: GET sends X-Revision, POST accepts optional baseRevision -> 409. Without baseRevision it stays last-write-wins (compatible with current pages). Shipping SO status writes left alone (Phase 6) but go through atomic writeJSONFile. Parking: bin lock check-then-lock is still two calls (TOCTOU) -> Phase 7.

[2026-10-29T23:40:01-04:00] result: server/store.js (atomic temp+fsync+rename, per-file queue, content-hash revision, ConflictError) + 9 unit tests; index.js wired: users create/put/delete and login writes, bin locks, /api/data GET X-Revision + POST baseRevision->409. New data-safety tests: against the OLD index.js 5 of 7 fail (parallel user creates and bin locks lost records, login could undo a concurrent admin edit); with the change all pass. Server total 46 pass, tsc ok. Left as-is: shipping SO status writes (Phase 6, now atomic anyway); bin lock check-then-lock is still two calls (TOCTOU, parking lot, Phase 7). Drift check: ok, server-only.
subtasks.testStrategy: node tests: interrupted write leaves old file readable; 50 parallel increments through the queue all land; stale baseRevision returns 409; existing data files still read

home-page.tsx, export-page.tsx, setup-page.tsx, settings-page.tsx, app.tsx, utils: replace localStorage business-data reads/writes; Home dashboard now computes from server data; Setup uploads write once through the layer.

[2026-10-30T00:08:24-04:00] plan/deviation: Scan and Inventory pages still read the localStorage mirror that app.tsx/setup/settings write until 10.6 converts them, so removing the mirror now would break those pages on this branch. Therefore 10.5 = (a) store option refresh:false for big static collections (rf_active, rf_master are MBs; no 30s polling for them) + saveCollection reload:false; (b) Home fully on useCollection (stats recompute as data refreshes); (c) Export on useCollection; (d) Setup: PO/SO uploads via upsertManyRecords (server-side merge, no client read-merge-write), inventory persist via saveCollection(overwrite) with visible failure instead of console-only; (e) Settings: master replace/reload via saveCollection with visible failure, master summary from server. The mirror writes stay, marked for removal in 10.6 together with app.tsx hydration and the Setup info-box wording. utils/config.ts rf_config_staging_bin and settings rf_app_settings are per-device preferences, not business data: stay in localStorage by design. NOTE for owner: 'Replace master inventory' rebuilds ALL bins from the file (existing behavior, confirm dialog) so it discards receipt/pick changes to bin quantities - unchanged here but more consequential now that bins are shared.

[2026-10-30T00:11:10-04:00] result: done with ONE DOCUMENTED DEVIATION from the test strategy (grep-clean): home-page and export-page have zero localStorage; setup-page/settings-page/app.tsx keep the browser mirror ONLY because Scan and Inventory still read it - their server saves are now conflict-aware/visible and moved to ops. Mirror removal is carried to 10.6. Changes: store retain({refresh:false}) + useCollection option + saveCollection reload:false (new unit test), Home on 8 collections (recomputes on refresh), Export on useCollection, Setup PO/SO import via server-side upsert-many (no client read-merge-write), Setup/Settings inventory replace via saveCollection with errors visible in the status line (Settings previously used Promise.all and could half-save; Setup swallowed errors into a console message). Checks with exit codes: tsc 0, vitest 28, build ok, server 67. New task 17 (guard destructive Setup actions, audit 4l) added because it was in no task. Drift check: no scope change except task 17.

subtasks.title: Convert Inventory and counting storage calls
subtasks.description: inventory-page.tsx and scan-page.tsx stop using localStorage for business data (storage calls only).
subtasks.details:
inventory-page.tsx (45 call sites), scan-page.tsx, numpad-modal as needed, keys rf_inventory_sessions, rf_current_inventory_session, rf_cycle_counts, rf_temporary_locations, rf_bins, rf_session_count_logs. No restructuring or splitting of the file (Phase 7).

[2026-10-30T00:15:11-04:00] plan: keep inventory-page handler logic intact, change only where data comes from/goes. (1) Server: RECORD_KEYS += rf_cycle_counts, rf_inventory_sessions, rf_temporary_locations (all have ids); APPEND_KEYS += rf_session_count_logs (entries get an id); new POST /api/records/:key/apply {upsert[],remove[]} (several record changes under one lock) and POST /api/ops/bins-set {newBins[],changes[{binCode,itemCode,description?,setQuantity}]} (all-or-nothing; counting is an absolute set, never a delta). (2) Client: src/data/diff.ts pure diffRecords/diffBins (unit tested) turn a handler's before/after arrays into just the changed records, so two counters on different bin ranges no longer overwrite each other; item/bin removal is refused loudly (no handler does it). (3) inventory-page: arrays come from useCollection; the existing setX(updated) calls become shims that persist the diff and toast on failure; the localStorage.setItem lines for business data are deleted; rf_current_inventory_session (which session THIS handheld is in) stays in localStorage on purpose. (4) scan-page, numpad-modal, shipping-page (storage calls only, shipping API untouched), sample-data (returns data; setup saves it), then remove the mirror from app.tsx/setup/settings. Known pre-existing issue left alone: inventory-page reads usernames from localStorage rf_users (never filled since users live on the server) so count logs say 'Unknown' -> parking lot.

[2026-10-30T00:23:28-04:00] result: no business-data localStorage left. Server: ops-logic/ops add records/:key/apply (several record changes, one lock), ops/bins-set (absolute quantities + new bins, all-or-nothing), RECORD_KEYS += cycle counts, sessions, temporary locations, APPEND_KEYS += session count logs; client: src/data/diff.ts (diffRecords/diffBins, 6 unit tests; removals refused), ops.saveRecordChanges/saveBinChanges. inventory-page: arrays from useCollection, the existing setX(updated) calls are shims that save only the changed records and toast on failure; 22 localStorage writes removed; the per-device pointer rf_current_inventory_session stays (and rf_users legacy read, parked). scan-page, numpad-modal (saveCollection, conflict-checked, shows 'Not saved'), shipping-page (orders via shared data; label API untouched), sample-data (now server-based; fills ONLY empty orders/waves/counts so it cannot replace real shared orders), app.tsx/setup/settings mirror removed, Setup info box now says data is on the server, unused useServerStorage deleted. localStorage that remains by design: rf_config_staging_bin, rf_current_inventory_session, rf_app_settings (per-device), legacy cleanup in clearAllData, demo backend storage. Tests (all exit codes checked): tsc 0, vitest 36 incl. two new two-device tests (two devices counting different bins at once keep all counts; two devices saving different sessions both land), build ok, server 72. REAL BROWSER CHECK: the repo's own scripts/e2e-preview.mjs (run from /tmp with global playwright, demo mode) passes fully - receiving, picking, inquiry, cycle count persistence, exports, shipping, mobile - with no console/page errors. It also caught a REGRESSION I introduced in 10.3: the sync pill pushed the mobile top bar to 437px (> 390 viewport); fixed (dot on phones, banner for errors), re-verified. Not verified: real handheld with the real API and real data.
